question: Which observed surface units can differ only in the two entry connectors of IDEA928, under the already fixed G1 surface segmentation?
binding: Each already stored G1 surface segment is a complete cell realization, with a unique observable LOW/HIGH entry and fixed body exit. Embedded c[kptf]h remains one surface segment, not BH/HB expansion. No motif split, null, merger or cell-dependent identity. Conditional symbolic binding, not established native letter atoms.
eligible_groups: Both complete group boundaries definite or physical line edge. Ignore uncertain groups; do not join them. All internal motif adjacencies in retained groups are included.
constraints: Each eligible word-first surface v has entry(v)=LOW.
For each observed adjacency u,v: exit(u)=entry(v).
For any tested same-body pair a,b: exit(a)=exit(b) and entry(a)!=entry(b). Distinct surfaces of one body must be its two connector realizations.
analysis: Equality components from entry/exit constraints; report forced LOW entries, all remaining free equality components, and necessary same-body pair compatibility. A component may independently be LOW or HIGH; no guessed letter table.
scope: 53 already exposed two-line reader records; readers separate. Pair enumeration is a necessary-condition census, not learned synonymy, score or a native body inventory.

decisions.no_compatible_pair: This fixed-cell realization can make no observed two-entry allographic identification; park it before a decoder.
decisions.some_compatible_pairs: Retain only as formal possibilities requiring a separately motivated common native body; do not select by feasibility.
decisions.specific_pair_conflict: Reject only this same-body assignment, not IDEA928 without a native inventory.
